slot.brief: A wire is stretched to double (or n-times) its length keeping volume constant; find new resistance and ratio of old to new resistance.

stem: A wire has resistance $3\ \Omega$. It is stretched uniformly to twice its original length, with its volume and resistivity unchanged. What is its new resistance?

verdicts.working: With volume constant, doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area. Since $R=\rho L/A$, the resistance becomes $4\times 3=12\ \Omega$.

working:
Constant volume gives $A'=A/2$.
$R'=\dfrac{\rho(2L)}{A/2}=4\dfrac{\rho L}{A}=4R=12\ \Omega$.

Independent check: With volume constant, doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area. Since $R=\rho L/A$, the resistance becomes $4\times 3=12\ \Omega$.
solution:
With volume constant, doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area: $A'=A/2$.
$$R'=\frac{\rho(2L)}{A/2}=4R=4(3)=12\ \Omega$$
